message: kandalī as "stalk of the throat" has no MW support (mw-kandali: deer, plant, banner…); only vyakhya (कण्ठ-नाल) and shlokam (stem) support it. sanskritdocuments' "temple" isn't recorded as an alternative.
suggested_fix: Point the sense at kandala "new shoot" used figuratively, and add the "temple" reading as an alternative.

message: Only the literal image (radiance of blue lotuses); the implied simile and its referent (the poison-darkened throat, Nīlakaṇṭha, per vyakhya-sts-9) are never stated.
suggested_fix: "whose neck shines with a throat dark like a mass of full-blown blue lotuses" + a note citing vyakhya-sts-9 on Nīlakaṇṭha.

message: Says MW knows kandalī 'only' as a flowering plant; mw-kandali lists five senses (deer, white-flowered plant, lotus seed, banner, title). Also 'avalambin means … bearing' presents an interpretation as MW's meaning (MW: hanging on, resting upon). The same 'only' claim is in words.w3.notes.
suggested_fix: 'MW gives no "stalk" sense for kandalī (it lists a deer, a white-flowered plant, lotus seed, a banner), so the stalk reading rests on vyakhya.org'; 'avalambin means resting on (MW); vyakhya glosses it "endowed with", hence "bearing" here.' Fix w3.notes too.
